title: DRFusion: Drift-Resilient Video Fusion
one_liner: Instead of trying to align frames with optical flow, DRFusion learns to predict each infrared-visible frame from its history, avoiding drift by treating fusion as motion generation.
lead: When you fuse infrared and visible video in real time, small mistakes pile up—a tiny blur in frame 1 becomes a ghostly smear by frame 10. Existing methods either lock frames in place with rigid alignment (which breaks in dynamic scenes) or process each frame alone (losing the motion context that keeps things steady). DRFusion fixes this by learning to generate the fused frame directly from what came before, treating fusion not as alignment but as conditional prediction.

problem.h2: The drift problem: mistakes that grow over time
paras: Fusing infrared (heat) and visible (color) video is hard because the two streams move differently. Infrared sees heat, visible sees edges—they do not naturally align.

Early methods tried optical flow (computing where pixels moved between frames) to keep alignment rigid. But optical flow breaks when motion is fast or objects are hidden—forced alignment creates ghosting artifacts and structural distortions.

Modern diffusion models (generative models that build images step by step) can fuse frames well in isolation, but when run frame-by-frame on a video without explicit temporal wiring, errors creep in. A small blur in frame 1 is not corrected by frame 2; instead, it is carried forward as a seed for the next blur. By frame 10, the video is unusable drift.

callout.html: Processing each video frame in a generative model without connecting it to the frame before it causes error accumulation—the model can generate beautiful single frames but has no intrinsic way to keep them temporally consistent.

steps.b: Stage 1: Train a noise-resistant compressed representation
steps.text: Compress both infrared and visible video to a dense numerical summary (a compressed representation, like reducing a photo to its essential numbers) while enforcing smooth motion between frames using optical flow hints—like a video autofocus that smooths frame-to-frame jitter.

steps.b: Stage 2: Teach the model to ignore flow, focus on history
steps.text: Train a lightweight adapter (a small numerical patch) on top of a frozen generative model so it learns to predict the fused frame from a sliding window of frames that came before it.

Repurpose the model's attention mechanism (the part that decides where to look) to create three overlapping windows of history. Each attention layer uses these windows as soft anchors—like three slightly shifted mirrors reflecting the same scene.
The overlapping windows implicitly filter out high-frequency noise (flickering) while preserving low-frequency motion (actual scene changes), without ever computing optical flow explicitly.
At inference, slightly nudge the fused image to preserve infrared structure (edges and textures) while keeping the temporal smoothness learned from history.

paras: The paper changes the architecture used to process video fusion: from independent frame-by-frame processing to history-conditioned prediction. Instead of a 2D model that sees each frame alone, DRFusion uses a 3D temporal model that explicitly encodes the previous frames (frames that came before the current one) as context.
object.object: temporal architecture: single frame to history-conditioned

hidden.h2: The hidden quantity: motion continuity score
hidden.name: Frame-to-frame optical flow prediction error
paras: The paper does not name a single hidden quantity but implicitly measures frame-to-frame consistency. DRFusion learns to predict the warping error (how much each pixel should shift between frames) using optical flow computed during Stage 1 training. In Stage 2, this error becomes implicit in the history windows.

The paper estimates this via temporal smoothness constraints on the latent space (the compressed representation) and validates it with metrics like structural similarity (SSIM) and temporal coherence scores across benchmark datasets.

heat.caption: Darker means stronger drift or constraint. Highlighted cells show active controls: drift without guidance (top), then anchoring windows and final stability (bottom).

reads.html: The model learns to recognize patterns in how frames shift and change over time. When it has seen the last two frames, it can predict what the next fused frame should look like without computing optical flow.

DRFusion minimizes occlusion-aware latent warping error during VAE training and implicitly models motion dynamics via self-attention repurposing (Soft Temporal Anchoring), where historical Keys and Values act as low-pass filters.

mechanism.h2: Why learning motion history beats rigid alignment
paras: Rigid optical flow breaks because it assumes pixels move in straight lines at constant speed—a false assumption when objects rotate, deform, or vanish. Forcing this assumption causes ghosting and structural artifacts.

DRFusion avoids the trap by learning the motion pattern implicitly. By conditioning on history, the generative model learns: when frames shift like this in the past, what does the next frame look like? The model discovers non-linear, scene-aware motion without being told.

The Soft Temporal Anchoring mechanism (three overlapping history windows passed to attention layers) acts as a low-pass filter. High-frequency jitter—tiny flickers that bounce around—gets averaged out across the windows. Low-frequency motion—genuine scene changes—passes through because it is consistent across all three windows. This is spectral filtering without rigid alignment.

Finally, the two-stage training decouples learning: Stage 1 builds a clean latent space (like a noise-free blueprint), and Stage 2 teaches the generative model to use it. This separation prevents the model from memorizing input noise and amplifying it over time.

stages.s: Infrared video stream, visible video stream
Compress to latent space with optical flow smoothing
Learn lightweight adapter on frozen generative model
Create three overlapping history windows (soft anchors)
Attention mechanism applies low-pass filtering across windows
Generate fused frame conditioned on motion history

math.words: occlusion_aware_latent_warping_loss = sum of (distance between compressed frame T and compressed frame T minus 1, warped by optical flow, weighted by occlusion mask)
symbols: the compressed summary of frame t
the compressed summary of the previous frame
optical flow: how each pixel moved from frame t-1 to frame t
warp operation: shift each pixel according to optical flow
occlusion mask: which pixels are hidden (1 = visible, 0 = hidden)
the mismatch penalty (how much the frames differ after flow-based alignment)

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Suppose the compressed representation encodes each frame as 100 numbers. At time t-1, frame is [0.5, 0.3, ..., 0.2].
At time t, frame is [0.52, 0.29, ..., 0.18]. Optical flow says pixel 1 moved +2 units right.
After warping the frame from before by flow, we get [0.5, 0.3, ..., 0.2]_warped.
Squared: [0.0004, 0.0001, ..., 0.0004]. Sum = 0.0008. This is L_warp—small because motion is smooth.
If the model produces erratic encodings (frame t is [0.9, 0.1, ..., 0.1]), squared difference is [0.16, 0.04, ..., 0.01], sum = 0.21—huge penalty.
During training, the model learns compressed representations that change predictably, avoiding abrupt jumps.

math.note: The latent space (compressed representation) is trained to evolve smoothly across frames. This gives the generative model a clean foundation—motion information is already baked in before the model even starts predicting.

bars.h2: Temporal consistency and fusion quality trade-off

charts.title: Rigid optical flow method
charts.note: Optical flow preserves fine details but cannot handle occlusions and fast motion, causing ghosting and temporal jitter.

charts.title: DRFusion (this paper)
charts.note: By learning motion dynamics implicitly via history conditioning, DRFusion maintains both spatial quality and temporal smoothness without rigid constraints.

items.html: If the initial compression is jerky (high-frequency jitter baked in), the history windows cannot filter it out. The model learns bad motion patterns from corrupted training data. Solution: pre-train the VAE on high-quality video first.

If the three overlapping windows are too small (e.g., only 1 frame back), they do not capture genuine motion and over-filter real changes, because a single frame before it is not enough to distinguish between random jitter and true motion. If too large, they include outdated context that contradicts the current frame. Solution: tune window size to scene dynamics (faster scenes need smaller windows because rapid motion changes quickly and old frames become misleading).

If the refinement step (nudging the fused image to preserve infrared edges) is too aggressive, it undoes the temporal smoothing. If too weak, infrared detail is lost. Solution: adaptive weighting based on local infrared contrast.
The model learns motion continuity without rigid constraints, attends to history without being locked to it, and preserves both temporal smoothness and structural fidelity.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build a small video fusion pipeline: download one sequence of aligned infrared and visible frames (e.g., from the M3SVD or HDO dataset), run the pre-trained model on 30 frames, and measure two things: (1) SSIM score between the fused frame and a ground-truth fused reference (structure quality), and (2) temporal stability via optical flow magnitude between consecutive fused frames (flickering metric).
demo.metric_eq: temporal_stability = mean(L1_distance(fused_{t}, fused_{t-1})) over all frames; lower = smoother. structural_quality = SSIM(fused_t, reference_t) over all frames; higher = better.
demo.closing: Run the same 30 frames through a naive frame-by-frame diffusion model (no history). The frame-by-frame version will have high SSIM but low temporal stability (many flickers). DRFusion should show: high SSIM AND high stability, proving that history conditioning filters jitter without sacrificing detail.
